remarks.role: Builder. Make something people want, then make people want it. Harvard’17. GitHub: https://t.co/KCuEaje1wd
remarks.text:
Never had so many AI products looked so similar

Even though the number of products is exploding, there aren't that many radical new ideas and everything blurs into each other

Every time I open this app it feels like homework: yet another new product to learn that promises to do the same thing but somehow better; the specific ways in which it's better isn't clear unless you invest hours actually trying it
remarks.translation: 从未有如此多的人工智能产品看起来如此相似。尽管产品数量激增，但真正颠覆性的新想法并不多，一切都趋于同质化。每次打开这个应用，感觉都像在做作业：又是一个新产品要学习，承诺做同样的事情却声称更好；但除非你投入数小时实际试用，否则它究竟好在哪并不清楚。

remarks.text:
Resist dunking*

I see it WAY too much with folks especially today. It’s the perfect dopamine loop - other people join in and you feel great. But, it just screams envy and doesn’t lead to anything productive. 

Sure, you can pat yourself on the back and say “see I told you so” but how did it move the world? Nowhere. If you think you can do it better, go do that then. Screaming about someone’s unfair advantages is not going to change your life - and probably leads to more sadness. 

Keep building. Continue to change the world. That’s the best way to have impact. Choose kindness above all else. 

* the only caveat here is if you’re calling out obvious fraud, or pointing out something that’s woefully bad, do it. there are very clearly some businesses that are going to be vaporware and if you have evidence call it out. that doesn’t scream envy, it’s factual and not dunking by any means.
remarks.translation: 抵制“扣篮式嘲讽”* 我见过太多人这样做了，尤其是今天。这是一个完美的多巴胺循环——其他人加入进来，你感觉很棒。但是，这只是在宣泄嫉妒，不会带来任何有成效的结果。当然，你可以拍拍自己的背说“看吧，我早就说过了”，但这如何推动了世界？毫无进展。如果你认为自己能做得更好，那就去做。对别人的不公平优势大喊大叫不会改变你的生活——而且很可能导致更多的悲伤。继续建设。继续改变世界。这才是产生影响的最佳方式。选择善良高于一切。* 这里唯一的例外是，如果你在揭露明显的欺诈，或者指出某些极其糟糕的事情，那就去做。很明显，有些企业注定是空壳产品，如果你有证据，就指出来。那不是在宣泄嫉妒，而是基于事实，绝不是“扣篮式嘲讽”。

remarks.name: Guillermo Rauch
remarks.role: vercel CEO
remarks.text:
https://t.co/OL0LzGtvAw 0.0.7: 

- hugely improved MCP support, eval'd with top MCPs like @context7ai, @datadoghq, @mongodb, @linear, @notionhq, @supabase, @neondatabase, @stagehanddev, @usekernel…

- more minimalist: fewer tools and improved shell execution. One of the trickiest things about CLI agents is that running commands is actually not that simple.

e.g: commands might hang or run for very long, their output needs to be monitorable by the agent, they might produce huge amounts of output, or none. 

This is an area where 𝚏𝚡 really shines and will continue to get better.
remarks.translation: https://t.co/OL0LzGtvAw 0.0.7：- 大幅改进的MCP支持，已与顶级MCP如@context7ai、@datadoghq、@mongodb、@linear、@notionhq、@supabase、@neondatabase、@stagehanddev、@usekernel等进行评估。- 更加简约：减少工具数量并改进shell执行。CLI代理最棘手的问题之一是，运行命令实际上并不简单。例如：命令可能会挂起或运行很长时间，其输出需要能被代理监控，它们可能产生大量输出，或完全没有输出。这是𝚏𝚡真正擅长的领域，并将持续改进。

podcasts.title: 🔬“我们有用于语言的基础模型，却没有用于物理学的基础模型” —— 阿尼玛·阿南德库马尔，布伦计算学教授
podcasts.originalTitle: 🔬“We have foundation models for language, not for physics” — Anima Anandkumar, Bren Professor of Computing
podcasts.excerpt: 几年前，加州理工学院教授、Accelerated Understanding联合创始人Anima Anandkumar着手开发首个基于AI的开源天气模型。在与该领域专家交流时，她遇到了质疑。天气是混沌的，物理模拟很难，已经发展了几十年，并且需要超级计算机，数据根本不够。尽管有这些保留意见，Anima还是坚持前行并开始构建。不到一年，她的团队就开发出了FourCastNet，一个能与现有最佳物理模拟相媲美的预测模型。多亏了Anima及其后续工作，现在任何人都可以使用消费级GPU在短时间尺度上准确预测天气。在我们发布的十五期左右的科学节目中，<a target="_blank" href="http://latent.…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: A few years ago, Caltech Prof. and co-founder of Accelerated Understanding, Anima Anandkumar set out to develop the first open-source weather model with AI. Talking to experts in the field, she was met with skepticism. Weather is chaotic, physics simulations are hard, have been developed for decades, and require supercomputers, the data just isn’t there. Despite reservations, Anima went forth and built. Within a year her team had developed FourCastNet, a predictive model that is competitive with the best physics-based simulations available. Thanks to Anima, and her follow up work, anyone can now predict weather accurately over a short timescale using consumer grade GPUs. In the fifteen or so science episodes we’ve released on <a target="_blank" href="http://latent.…
